hero.title: The salmon we produce and consume

bomb.title: ARE ECOLOGICAL, SOCIAL AND HEALTH BOMBS

impact.title: Every year in France, we consume 37.6 million salmon
impact.impact: (the equivalent in tons of 19 Eiffel Towers)
impact.title2: of these millions of salmon, 98% are farmed
impact.description: Unlike a large part of the fish we consume, 98% of the salmon consumed in France are farmed. We do not catch them. We feed them, every day, for two years, in cages.

menuCards.title: Wild fish, reduced to meal and oil
menuCards.content: Salmon is a carnivorous fish. In farming, they are small wild fish caught and processed into meal and oil to feed the salmon. This fishing causes accidental catches of sharks, turtles, whales...

menuCards.title: Soy, wheat, rapeseed
menuCards.content: Salmon are carnivorous fish, yes... but also fed with soy. The crops used to feed salmon occupy a larger area than Paris + Hauts-de-Seine + Seine-Saint-Denis combined!

menuCards.title: Krill, fished in Antarctica
menuCards.content: To enhance its pink color, we also give it krill, this tiny shrimp that is the food of many animals in the Antarctic ecosystem.

menuCards.title: Anti-parasitic treatments
menuCards.content: To keep salmon alive and healthy, we administer anti-parasite treatments; mainly against sea lice, small crustaceans that proliferate in farms.

menuCards.title: Microplastics
menuCards.content: Farmed salmon can ingest microplastics present in their environment or their food.

menuCards.title: Eternal pollutants
menuCards.content: The food used in aquaculture can be a pathway for fish exposure to PFAS.

item1.title: Wastewater from 2.9 million people:
item1.description: Everything given to farmed salmon does not become flesh. The rest comes out: excrement, uneaten feed, treatment residues. This activity represents up to the equivalent of the untreated wastewater produced by 2.9 million people.

item2.title: Resources for 588 million people:
item2.description: The food fed to farmed salmon is sourced from waters off countries where fish are among the few accessible sources of protein. Sardines, anchovies, sardinella... whole fish, caught specifically to be ground up. These diverted resources could meet the protein needs of 588 million people.

item3.title: 398 microplastics:
item3.description: In France, each person consumes an average of 3.8 kg of farmed salmon per year, which is equivalent to ingesting around 398 microplastics every year.

item4.title: Less omega-3:
item4.description:
For your information: Omega-3s do not come from salmon. They come from the algae that fish used to consume.

Today, salmon flesh contains significantly less omega-3.

Pollutants, however, accumulate.
